missionItem4Resolution.decision: RETIRED AS A CONTROL, kept as an INSTRUMENT. Not wired.
missionItem4Resolution.whyNotWired: evaluatePublishGate is a whole-county gate over records that must each carry all 65 rails (assertFullRecordCells); the publish path's rail half reads per-(county, rail) rows written per rail by a subprocess. Wiring it would require fabricating the other 64 rails per record -- which corrupts deriveLiveRailKeys' cross-record liveness, the reason PARCEL-B-GATE-SCHED was built -- or duplicate an already-correct decision with a second implementation. The publish path is not ungated: RAIL_UNACCOUNTED, RAIL_REFUSED, RAIL_EXCLUSION_UNPROVEN.
missionItem4Resolution.enforcement: test/gate-caller-registry.test.mjs parses every gate-shaped export from the engine index and the readiness gate, requires each to be registered (publish-control | instrument | uncalled) or explicitly declared not-a-gate, asserts the classification agrees with where the symbol actually sits relative to the publish path, and asserts the declared caller list EQUALS the src/ files that reference the symbol in code (comments stripped -- a header that merely discusses a gate cannot satisfy the registry). A new exported gate with undeclared caller status fails, and so does wiring a retired gate in without updating the registry.
missionItem4Resolution.whatTheRegistrySays: evaluatePublishGate + poisonCell = instrument (parcel-record-fill.mjs's POISON_GATE_VACUOUS self-test, still asserted to exist); assertPublishableCounty + allRailKeys = uncalled; evaluateRailGate, requirePreBakeReadiness, evaluatePreBakeReadiness, requireCountyPopulation, evaluatePopulation, classifyExclusion = publish controls.

Asserted structurally instead, by enumerating the neighbouring shapes and where they land (test/p252-zero-earned-refusal.test.mjs, 'STRUCTURAL (dry run UNMEASURED)'): declared-ahead+unaccounted -> exclusion (unchanged); declared-ahead+zero cells -> exclusion (unchanged); live+zero cells -> RAIL_NEVER_FILLED (P-195); live+all not-applicable -> exclusion; live+all earned -> pass; live+one unaccounted among earned -> refuse on the PRE-EXISTING path with no new code; live+no earned+unaccounted -> the new code. The new code is therefore reachable for exactly one shape, which is the falsifier's content stated as code structure rather than as a store measurement.
dryRun.publishFloorConsequence_NAME_THIS: PUBLISH FLOOR CONSEQUENCE, derived from code read at source (not measured): maxImperviousCoverPct is in PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS (SLATE_1B) and its writer (parcel-max-impervious-cover.mjs) refuses COUNTY_NOT_IN_SCOPE for every county but Travis and writes NO cell state there -- so its cells in Bastrop, Caldwell, Hays, McLennan and Williamson are unaccounted, which under P-252 is a refusal. Consequence: after the scheduler runs under the new code, requirePreBakeReadiness will refuse a publish for all five non-Travis counties of the six on that floor rail alone. agValuation's expected refusals (Bastrop, Caldwell, Hays, McLennan) are NOT floor rails and cannot refuse a publish by themselves. The remedy is the out-of-scope not-applicable sweep reaching those counties (writeAgValuationNotApplicable is the precedent) -- a data/writer action this lane is forbidden to take (P-266/P-267) and does not take.
